reasoning_traces.think: Chapter 1 introduces a foundational challenge in modern football analytics: the context-dependence of player impact. Traditional metrics fail because they treat actions as static indicators of ability, ignoring how performance varies across tactical environments. This motivates a shift toward dynamic, context-aware models such as Expected Possession Value (EPV), Expected Threat (xT), and On-Ball Value (OBV). These frameworks recognize that value is not intrinsic to an action but emerges from its interaction with game state. The paper proposes EventGPT, a GPT-style autoregressive model conditioned on player identity and game state, to simulate how a player’s presence alters the trajectory of events. This approach enables counterfactual analysis—evaluating what would happen if a player were replaced—thereby addressing the core problem of transfer fit. The framework integrates SPADL for structured event representation and leverages large-sequence modeling techniques from natural language processing. It bridges the gap between static scouting and dynamic performance prediction by embedding player-specific behavior into event prediction models. The implications extend beyond transfer evaluation to real-time tactical decision-making and squad composition optimization.
